_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
EVERY FIELD HAS A WORD CAP, and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build past it:
name 16, why 40, risk 80, touches 80, note 120, comment 120, askedBy.detail 80. A
session with more to say than that puts it in the feature's Brief or history file
and links it. ONE FACT, ONE HOME: replace a sentence that is out of date; never append
an UPDATED paragraph beneath it. On 2026-09-03 one item's comment had grown to 1,388
words across seven sessions that way, and Mike could not read his own list.
activeOn: { machine, since } says which computer is working an item right now —
'laptop' or 'desktop', from the date given. Mike's instruction, 2026-09-03, after item
4.54 was built on both machines in the same week. Absent means nobody is on it. The
page shows it as a column, the control shows it on the row, and the control's save
carries it through. Shutdown clears or keeps it; startup reports the other machine's.
rankedByMike: false marks an item filed after orderedByMikeOn that Mike has not yet
placed. The page and the Handbook control show it. It clears itself: the control's
export does not carry the field, so his next saved list drops it.
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.
orderSource: the Handbook ranking control (scripts/handbook-shell.html), saved by Mike on 2026-08-15. It replaced design/mockups/to-do-list-table.html, which set the order before it.

On a developer machine the activity store falls back to a dev file and the write silently does not happen, so this is a two-minute look in UAT: open the Team tab as a firm manager after a real session and compare its templates and tier with the conversation. items.name: A point the mentor adds tells a firm manager THEY wrote it
items.why: A firm manager who has customised nothing sees "Added here" against every observation point the mentor wrote, because the resolver returns the layer above untouched.
items.risk: It reads as authorship. A firm manager is told they added a point they cannot edit and did not write, which is the opposite of what the badge exists to say — and the badge is what tells them whether a correction of theirs is safe from the mentor's later changes. It looks completely normal on screen, which is why nobody has reported it.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-09-02 while building the meeting TYPES cascade, whose resolver had the identical fault — fixed there, and deliberately NOT patched here, because the points are a shipped screen and their own change. Nobody outside asked; it is filed because a defect we find is still a defect.

items.touches: server/utils/meetingObservations.js (the no-decisions passthrough in loadResolvedObservations) and tests/unit/meetingObservations.test.js. The fix is the one already made in server/utils/meetingTypes.js: restamp the inherited list from the viewer's point of view. Both paths — passthrough and full resolve — must agree, or the badge flickers with unrelated edits.
items.comment: 2026-09-02 — one line plus two assertions, and the fix is already written and proven in the sibling module. Left undone only to keep slice 2 of the types cascade to its approved scope.

items.name: QuickBooks and MYOB are supported on paper, not against a real file
items.why: The reader now names QuickBooks Online and MYOB as supported, but both were tested only against reconstructed layouts; no real export from either has been read.
items.risk: A reconstruction proves the reader copes with the documented layout, not that the layout is right; the real Xero exports refuted three assumptions. A plausible wrong opening balance is exactly what UAT cannot catch. Every intake screen says the two are unconfirmed and tags each seeded figure by its source.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-02 — "keep it as a job for future - keep moving forward", after being told that four real exports are what would move the two packages from `expected` to `verified`.

The five defects the reconstructions found are in report-models.md §4b. Do not promote either package on more reconstructions: the guard in accountingPackages.test.js refuses `verified` without a named real export.

items.name: Two years of accounts, and a volatility read, for the forecast
items.why: Mike asked to drop two years of Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet for basic trend analysis including volatility; today the forecast reads one year from one file.
items.risk: Nothing is broken while this is undone. The risk is in the doing: the comparative-column work touches the guard that stops a two-year file being read as one year, and a figure from the wrong year is completely believable.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-03 — "i also think we need the ability to drop the last 2 years worth of p&l and balance sheet so some basic trend analysis can be performed - including volatility analysis - for which we have calcs model already - perhaps in next phase of this build?" Asked while approving the forecast's three data-entry screens.

items.touches: For (a): server/routes/report.js, server/report/intake/threeWayForecastAssembler.js, components/ThreeWayForecastIntake.vue and its test. For (b): server/report/intake/xeroReportParser.js, and a drawing of its own first.
items.note: Two pieces. (a) Volatility needs 24 months, not two years, and the two-file monthly join is already built (monthlySeriesAssembler), so this is a connection from the forecast's step 1 to it, with no new arithmetic. (b) The annual trend read is new work and needs its own approved drawing before the parser's multi-column guard is touched. Do (a) first. Not gated on anything since PR #55 closed on 2026-09-03. Nothing written yet. Detail in report-models.md §4b.

items.name: Saved reports per client — so a client can edit what the advisor opened
items.why: Mike's request of 2026-09-03: once an advisor opens a model to a client, the client edits it and every edit is made clear. Nothing can be edited until a report is saved per client per model, which nothing does today.
items.risk: Without it the stub shows a client an open model with sample figures only. With it, a client's figure reaches an advisor's screen; the badge, banner and Restore (D4) are what stop a client edit passing as the advisor's.
